subject: Post-call: model evals & multilingual quality - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.muller@globexretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:18:00Z
Subject: Post-call: model evals & multilingual quality - next steps

Hi Anna / team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good conversation and helpful context on the multilingual QA needs across EU and APAC stores. Quick recap + proposed next steps: 

Recap:
- Primary goals: improve localized product descriptions and customer support reply quality in DE/FR/ES (EU) and JA/KO/HI (APAC); reduce hallucination on price/availability questions; maintain latency <= 250ms p50 for short replies.
- Current concerns: your internal evals showed a ~6-8% drop in German accuracy vs. English on the same prompt set.
- Data: you confirmed we can use an anonymized sample of ~2k utterances per locale for a focused eval.

Recommended short plan (we can run this as a scoped eval):
1) Baseline run (3 model variants):
   - Llama-3-70B (quantized q4_0) — quality baseline
   - Mistral-Chat-34B (float16) — latency/quality tradeoff
   - RedModel-40B-opt (our optimized runtime variant) — production candidate
2) Prompt set: use attached multilingual_prompt_set_v2.csv + your sample utterances (please upload to the Drive link below).
3) Metrics: exact match / intent accuracy / hallucination rate / latency p50/p95.
4) Timeline: 5 business days after we receive sample data and confirm regions (EU / APAC).

Attachments: multilingual_prompt_set_v2.csv, benchmark_summary_globex.pdf (summary of prior benchmark where we saw the DE regression).

Next steps / asks for Globex:
- Confirm you can share anonymized samples (2k per locale) by EOD 2026-11-23.
- Confirm priority locales (if fewer than the list above).
- Any hard latency SLA or on-prem constraints we should be aware of?

I've also added Neha and Rachel to help scope the eval and handle infra/region questions. We'll run the tests in the EU region first and mirror to APAC if results look good.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Date: 2026-11-21T07:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: model evals & multilingual quality - next steps

Thanks Marissa — we can share anonymized samples but need sign-off from legal on the APAC set (Japan). I'll push for the EU samples by 11/23 as requested. Attaching a small sample export (globex_locale_samples_20261121.csv) so you can see format.

Questions from our side:
- For EU we run in AWS eu-west-1; for APAC we'd prefer a Singapore or Tokyo region — can you confirm latency estimates for the RedModel-40B-opt in those regions? Particularly p95 for 128-token responses when using q4 quantization.
- If the DE accuracy issue is confirmed, will you be able to run a quick prompt-tuning sweep (5-7 configs) as part of the eval or is that an extra engagement?

Thanks — Anna
Anna Müller
Head of Localization, Globex Retail
anna.muller@globexretail.com
+49 30 1234 5678
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-11-23T14:06:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: model evals & multilingual quality - next steps

Anna — thanks for the sample. Confirming a few details:

- Latency: rough estimates for RedModel-40B-opt on Redwood Dedicated (eu-west-1 / ap-southeast-1): p50 ~120-160ms, p95 ~280-350ms for 128-token responses when running q4 quantized; float16 variants are ~1.7-2x slower p50 but p95 approaches 500ms depending on concurrency. We'll capture precise numbers in the baseline run.
- Prompt tuning: we can include a small prompt-sweep (5 configs) as part of the scoped eval — we'll flag it as an "eval add-on" but it's included in this phase (no extra contract required for the baseline sweep).
- Regions: we'll execute baseline in eu-west-1 and a Tokyo endpoint (ap-northeast-1) unless you prefer Singapore. Please confirm.

Timeline and next steps:
- If you upload the anonymized samples to the Drive folder (link below) by EOD 11/24, we can start the baseline and share results by 11/30.
- I'll follow up with Neha to confirm infra (region & routing) and with Rachel on evaluation metrics/visualization.

Drive link: https://drive.redwoodinternal.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-globex-multilingual-evals

Marissa

---

Date: 2026-11-25T16:12:00Z
Subject: RE: Post-call: model evals & multilingual quality - next steps

Quick internal runbook for the scoped eval (adding here for tracking):

1) Data intake: agree format from globex_locale_samples_20261121.csv; Marissa to confirm upload to Drive by EOD 11/24.
2) Infra: reserve 2 nodes eu-west-1 (Redwood Dedicated) + 1 node ap-northeast-1 for Tokyo; set burst policy so we can parallelize locale runs.
3) Models & configs:
   - model-A: Llama-3-70B-q4_0 + default tokenizer
   - model-B: Mistral-Chat-34B-fp16
   - model-C: RedModel-40B-opt (runtime kernel tuned) q4_0 + kv-cache enabled
   - prompt-sweep: 5 small permutations (temperature, system instruction variants, retrieval prefix)
4) Metrics: exact match, intent accuracy, hallucination rate (manual sampling + heuristic), latency p50/p95 per region, token cost estimate.
5) Deliverables: PDF summary + interactive dashboard link + recommended production config.
6) Timeline: 5 business days after data receipt; estimate completion by 2026-11-30 if samples arrive by 11/24.

I've opened a temporary eval job id: EV-GLX-20261125 and will assign to infra team once Marissa confirms. Vivek — can you confirm node reservations and estimated cost delta for q4 vs fp16?

Neha Kapoor
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
